sentences.text: The genus Vayuraptor contains only one known species, Vayuraptor nongbualamphuensis, which is known from a partial skeleton.
This animal was a mid-sized theropod estimated to be between 4 and 4.5 meters in length.
As a possible megaraptoran, Vayuraptor likely possessed a long snout, large claws, a light body, and long slender legs.
The manual phalanx of Vayuraptor lacks distinct extensor pits on the upper proximal surface, a trait found only in coelurosaurs.
The generic name Vayuraptor means "wind thief", derived from the Hindu god of wind Vayu and the Latin word for thief.
The left tibia of Vayuraptor is complete, long, and slender, featuring an expanded cnemial crest.
Fossils of Vayuraptor were discovered in 1988 by Paladej Srisuk at Phu Wat Site A1 in Nong Bua Lamphu Province, Thailand, and are now stored in the Sirindhorn Museum.
The name Vayuraptor was chosen because its long and gracile tibia suggests the animal was very fast and agile.
The specific name nongbualamphuensis is named after the Nong Bua Lamphu Province where the dinosaur was found.
In a 2019 description, Novas et al. recovered Vayuraptor as a coelurosaurian in a trichotomy with megaraptorans and tyrannoraptorans.
Vayuraptor lived during the Barremian stage, approximately 125.77 to 121.4 million years ago.
Vayuraptor likely shared its habitat with dinosaurs such as Phuwiangvenator, Kinnareemimus, Siamosaurus, Siamotyrannus, and Phuwiangosaurus.
